facility_roles.quote: experiment at the Material and Life Science Facility (MLF) of J-PARC is designed to directly test

intervals.label: proposal submitted to the J-PARC PAC
intervals.note: Start from the collaboration's page (proposal submitted to the J-PARC PAC in September 2013); the end is the stage-1 approval of April 2015 (next interval).
intervals.quote: The experimental proposal was submitted to the J-PARC PAC on September 2013 officially.

intervals.label: stage-1 approval to start of construction
intervals.note: Stage-1 approval. The collaboration's news page records that the PAC (26th meeting, minutes opened 2018-10) recommended stage-2 approval ('real go-sign of the experiment'); end date is the start of detector construction at J-PARC (news item 2017.12).
intervals.quote: On April 2015, the J-PARC E56 (JSNS2 : J-PARC Sterile Neutrino Search using neutrinos from J-PARC Spallation Neutron Source) experiment officially obtained stage-1 approval from J-PARC.

intervals.label: detector construction and installation
intervals.note: Start from the news item dated 2017.12; end is the first data taking (commissioning run, 2020-06-05).
intervals.quote: The part of the detector construction work is started at J-PARC.

intervals.label: commissioning run and refilling
intervals.note: First data on 2020-06-05, a 10-day commissioning run (5-15 June 2020, per arXiv:2111.07482); the detector was then refilled and re-installed in December 2020. End is the start of the first long physics run.
intervals.quote: We started to take data from June-5. The first physics run (the commissioning run) will be continued for 10 days.

intervals.label: long physics runs with the 24 m detector
intervals.note: First long run 2021-01-12 to June 2021; further long runs from 2022-01-28, spring 2023 and 2023-12-07 are listed on the same page. The Feb 2026 first-results paper says data taking is ongoing.
intervals.quote: In 2021-Jan, we start the first long term physics run (Jan-12).

lineage.note: JSNS2 is designed as a direct test of the LSND anomaly; it uses a different (spallation, mercury-target) muon-decay-at-rest source and a Gd-loaded scintillator. Row on the lexicographically smaller id, A1.
lineage.quote: JSNS2 offers the ultimate direct test of the LSND anomaly.

website.quote: The first results on sterile neutrino search using 2022 data was published.

name: JSNS2
notes: Phase II (JSNS2-II): a second, 48 m far detector built from 2021 (stainless-steel tank 10 m high, 8 m diameter; acrylic vessel installed 2024-02, scintillator filled July-August 2024, per the collaboration's news page); it is not a separate entity here.
Proton beam: 3 GeV protons from the J-PARC Rapid Cycling Synchrotron on the MLF mercury target (25 Hz, two 100 ns bunches).

physics_goals.quote: JSNS2 offers the ultimate direct test of the LSND anomaly.
physics_goals.value: Directly test the LSND anomaly (an excess of electron antineutrinos, a sterile-neutrino signal at about 1 eV^2) with muon-decay-at-rest antineutrinos at a 24 m baseline

summary.plain: A neutrino detector on the third floor of J-PARC's neutron and muon facility in Japan. It listens for antineutrinos from muons stopping in a mercury target, to test whether a fourth, sterile kind of neutrino explains an unexplained excess seen long ago at the LSND experiment.
summary.technical: Short-baseline (24 m) anti-nu_mu to anti-nu_e appearance search with muon-decay-at-rest antineutrinos from 3 GeV protons on the MLF mercury target (25 Hz, 1 MW design power reached 2024). Gd-loaded (0.1 %) liquid scintillator, 17 t fiducial, 50 t scintillator in all; inverse-beta-decay signal with delayed Gd-capture gammas. First results (2022 data): 2 events observed, 2.3 +- 0.4 expected background, 1.1 +- 0.5 expected from the LSND anomaly; a 48 m second detector (JSNS2-II) is built.
